newsitem.title: USA: Olympic sees no material impact from lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Olympic sees no material impact from lawsuit.

text.p: Olympic Financial Ltd said Thursday it does not expect a class-action lawsuit filed in Texas regarding car loan pricing to have a material impact on the company.

"The company has reviewed the allegations contained in this lawsuit and does not believe that this litigation will have a material adverse effect on the company's financial condition or results of operations," Olympic said in a news release pertaining to a modification of a senior note offering.
The company said its understanding is that under Texas law, the maximum damages recoverable if a class of car buyers was certified by the court would not exceed $200,000 total.

The lawsuit alleges that the plaintiff's new car loan was originated by a dealer at an annual percentage rate 0.1 percent above the 18 percent allowed by Texas law and then assigned to Olympic, which finances auto loans.
Olympic said it has reviewed all its loans purchased since its inception and for about 2,500 of the approximately 470,000 loans purchased, the interest rate exceeded legal maximums.
This resulted primarily from fees added to the company's "buy rate," Olympic said.

The company said it would take action against dealers regarding the loans where appropriate, and that it is likely to repurchase any such loans owned by securitization trusts. Those loans may be resecuritized, Olympic said.
Olympic shares were down 1/8 at 10 Thursday.
